note: Twelve curated real dogs, real listings. The two example-* entries below are synthetic, carry synthetic true, and exist only to show the shape. Search refuses synthetic entries so they can never reach a player. Every real entry needs: provider id, real listing_url, description_html copied verbatim from the listing, at least 200 chars of text after html strip or the pool filter drops it, photo_url kept as provenance and photo_local pointing into cache/photos/, org present in organizations, status as the listing says it now, ACTIVE unless a hand check found otherwise, and adopted_on copied from the page when the status is ADOPTED_CONFIRMED, retrieved_at set to the curation moment, synthetic left out. Shelter photos are never committed: cache/ is gitignored and make fetch-photos rebuilds it from photo_url on a fresh clone. Example photo files intentionally do not exist. age_text and weight_text are optional, verbatim from the listing, left out when the listing does not say. long_stay is set only when the provider files the dog as a long stay animal, verified by the curator at retrieval: it becomes a structured fact, never a claim about how many days. long_stay_evidence says how we know, placement for a catalog section or listing sentence for words on the page, and the loader rejects one without the other. A catalog heading is navigation and stays out of the description, the placement is still a fact. A listing sentence stays in the description as well, the flag is additive. listing_url must resolve to this one dog, a catalog or search page is not a listing: the org url is where a shelter page belongs. curation_note is a reminder to a future curator, ignored by the loader like the rest of the curation metadata. Each org carries source_style, templated or personal: curation metadata only, the loader ignores it on purpose so it can never reach a player, it exists so the set can be checked for how many dogs are described as themselves rather than as a category. After curation read each sanitized description once, stray angle brackets in listing text can swallow words.

dogs.name: Biscuit
dogs.description_html:
Meet Biscuit! This three year old lab mix is the whole package. She loves tennis balls, belly rubs and long sniffy walks around the yard.

Biscuit is a bit shy on her first day but warms up fast once she trusts you. She walks nicely on leash, knows sit, and settles quietly at night. Staff say she greets every morning with a full body wag.

dogs.name: Pepper
dogs.description_html:
Pepper is a nine year old beagle mix with the softest ears in the building and a nose that has never met a smell it did not like.

  • Housetrained and gentle
  • Happy to nap while you work
  • Walks slow, sniffs everything, wags at strangers

Pepper came to us as a stray, so his story before the shelter is unknown. What we know for sure: he loves crunchy treats and sunny spots.

dogs.name: Bella
dogs.description_html:
My family moved and could not keep me, so I came to Animal Humane Society to find a new home.

I'm a high energy, playful dog. I'll need plenty of physical activity, mental stimulation, and ongoing training to help me grow into a well-mannered companion.

I'm an affectionate dog that loves being close and sharing snuggles. I may need a little time to feel fully comfortable in a new space, but a home with moderate activity will help me settle in.

I’m a little uncomfortable around other animals at first and require extra time, patience, and space when I am introduced to resident pets. I need to get used to other animals slowly and in small steps.

I don’t like to share valuable items or my food with other people or pets and have trouble when items are taken away from me. I will need my family to manage this behavior.

dogs.name: Preston
dogs.description_html:
Another shelter was caring for me before I came to Animal Humane Society to find a home.

I'm a very energetic, playful dog who loves to stay busy. I will need exercise, mental stimulation, and obedience training to provide appropriate outlets for my energy.

I like playing with toys and enjoy other busy interactions. Playful dogs like me enjoy a good game of fetch or just quietly chewing on a stuffed animal. No matter which toy I choose, I want my new family to join me in the fun.

I had one of my legs surgically removed due to an injury. I’m getting around ok but I’m adjusting to balancing on 3 legs. In a few weeks, I’ll be completely healed and ready to run.

Hi, I’m Venus, and I have two settings: Velcro and Extra Velcro.

When I first arrived in foster care, the world was a very suspicious place. Coffee makers? Terrifying. My reflection in the window? Clearly an intruder. Snow shovels? Absolutely not. Coming from a neglectful situation, everything was new, confusing, and a little scary. But look at me now! I've blossomed into a confident, adventurous girl who's ready to take on the world... as long as my people come with me.

My daily schedule is pretty simple. Mornings are for sleeping in, cuddling in bed, and supervising couch snuggles. Afternoons are when I unleash my inner athlete with yard time, training sessions, short walks, fetch, and occasional zoomie explosions that end with me dramatically collapsing in the dirt wearing my signature pittie grin. Evenings? Those are reserved exclusively for cuddling. I take my cuddle responsibilities very seriously.

I love my humans more than words can describe. At first, I followed them so closely I was practically attached to their ankles. Now I'm secure enough to relax nearby while still keeping them under constant surveillance. I firmly believe physical contact is a basic necessity, and if you stop petting me, I will assume you've simply forgotten and remind you immediately. I also give world-class hugs and fully expect them in return.

Meeting new people is exciting! I'll happily say hello on walks, though visitors entering my home might get a cautious inspection before earning my approval. As for other dogs, my feelings are... complicated. Sometimes I'm friendly, sometimes I'm overwhelmed, and sometimes I make very poor decisions about expressing my excitement. Because of my history and previous experiences with other dogs, I would thrive as your one-and-only furry companion where I can focus all my love on my people.

I'm crate trained, potty trained, bath approved, and highly motivated by treats and praise. In fact, if you tell me I'm a good girl, my entire face lights up like I just won the lottery. I know my toys belong to me and usually leave your belongings alone, although I still occasionally check the counters to make sure no snacks have mysteriously appeared. My foster family would also like you to know that squeakers and tennis balls are not safe from me.

One of my funniest habits is my highly specialized method of showing affection. Most dogs give kisses. Not me. I like to carefully press my nose against your face, ear, or neck and take a long, dramatic sniff as if I'm conducting important scientific research. It's weird. It's adorable. It tickles.

If there's one thing you should know about living with me, it's this: I don't just want to be part of your life—I want to be your favorite part of every day. I deserve a home where I can be spoiled, adored, and treated like the center of the universe. In return, I'll give you endless loyalty, laughter, cuddles, and enough love to make up for all the years I went without it.

Professional Cuddle Inspector, Amateur Scent Detective, and Full-Time Good Girl

dogs.description_html:

Sugar Bear is a tiny senior gentleman with a huge heart and a very important mission: to become someone's favorite lap warmer!

When Sugar first arrived in foster care, he was understandably overwhelmed and completely shut down. He wouldn't eat or drink for two days and wanted nothing more than to stay glued to his foster. But what a difference a little time and security have made! Sugar is now eating well, exploring the house, greeting people with a happy wag, and showing everyone what a sweet little companion he can be.

Sugar is a calm, affectionate boy who loves being close to his people. He'll happily come over for pets, enjoys a morning belly rub, and sleeps with his foster. He's especially active in the morning, when he enjoys his daily walk and strolls beautifully on leash. Afterward, he's perfectly happy to settle in for a long, cozy nap.

He's also doing wonderfully with new people now that he's feeling more comfortable. Sugar greets strangers with a wagging tail and is even comfortable being picked up. He's a little independent in his own way, but he definitely likes knowing where his person is. If you disappear somewhere he can't follow, he'll let you know with a bark until you're back in sight.

Sugar isn't much of a toy guy, preferring companionship and exploring to playtime. He does, however, enjoy keeping tabs on the resident cats. He's fascinated enough to follow them over the baby gate and occasionally needs his foster to rescue him when he forgets how to get back. Naturally, he waits until his person notices and then politely requests a lift with a bark. Senior dogs know how to delegate!

Sugar is 100% potty-pad trained and is learning the ins and outs of going potty outside. After just a week, he's already about 50/50, so he's making progress as he adjusts to a new routine after previously living entirely indoors.

Sugar Bear is looking for someone who appreciates the quieter joys of life and has plenty of time to spend getting cozy. He doesn't need a marathon runner or an adventure junkie—he needs a warm lap, a soft place to nap, a gentle morning walk, and someone who will appreciate having a tiny shadow nearby. If you're looking for a sweet senior companion who will happily curl up beside you and make your home feel a little warmer, Sugar Bear is ready to be your perfect little lap warmer. 🐻💕

Jake is a little, sweet, devoted boy who absolutely adores his people. He forms strong bonds with the humans he loves and will happily follow you wherever you go. As soon as you sit down, Jake is ready to hop into your lap for some quality snuggle time. He’ll settle in for a cozy nap or enjoy a bone or toy while cuddled up beside you.

Jake gets along well with other dogs and enjoys having canine companions, making him a wonderful addition to a home with friendly resident pups. He’s not a very active guy, but he does enjoy a run around the yard during potty breaks and soaking up the sunshine on the deck.

Jake is almost fully potty trained and does great free-roaming when his family is away. He is a loud barker a little guy so he may not be a good fit for a living space with shared walls.

If you’re looking for a small, loyal, loving companion who will be devoted to his family, Jake may be your perfect match. He’s ready to become your new best friend!

Hi there! My name is Keno, and I'm a goofy, lovable guy who loves spending time with my humans. If we meet for the first time, I might be a little shy because strangers can make me nervous. I do best with slow introductions, especially since fast movements from people I don't know can startle me. Once I know you're safe, though, get ready—I become your biggest fan! I'll happily shower you with hugs, kisses, and snuggles, and I'd love nothing more than curling up beside you or sleeping by your side.

One of my favorite things to do is go for walks and follow every interesting scent I can find. Deer, cats, squirrels—you name it, I want to know where they've been! Because of my strong prey drive, I'll need someone who can keep me safely on leash during our adventures. At home, I love chew toys and stuffed Kongs, and I'm always ready to make you laugh with my silly personality. I even like racing my foster dad to the bed so I can steal his spot first. It's one of my favorite games!

I'm a smart boy who already knows some basic commands and enjoys learning new things. I'm still working on my potty training, and I can be pretty vocal if I'm left in my crate, but with patience and consistency, I keep making progress. I also have a habit of playfully using my paws when I'm excited, though we're working on redirecting that into better manners. If you're looking for an intelligent, affectionate, and endlessly entertaining companion who will keep you smiling and always guessing what goofy thing I will do next, I just might be your perfect match!

dogs.name: Lori
dogs.breed: Australian Shepherd / Australian Cattle Dog (Blue Heeler)
dogs.description_html:

  • Energy level high
  • Crate Trained
  • Does well in a car

Hi, I'm Lori! 🐾💕

Life is one big adventure, and I'm determined not to miss a single second of it! I'm a happy, energetic puppy with a motor that just keeps going. If you're looking for a couch potato...keep scrolling. But if you want a goofy best friend who will fill your days with fun, laughter, and endless tail wags, I'm your girl!

Meeting new people is my absolute favorite thing. My whole body wiggles when I see someone new, and I might even let out an excited little bark just to say, "Hi! Come play with me!" I love being around my people and always want to know what you're doing. You'll usually find me hanging out at your feet or stretched out on the couch nearby—just don't expect me to cuddle too close because I like to claim my personal lounging space!

When it comes to playtime, I'm all in! Toys? Love them all. Other dogs? Even better! I play like the cattle dog puppy I am, using my voice, chasing my friends around, and trying to "herd" them with playful nips at their feet and lots of mouthy wrestling. Because I'm still learning good puppy manners, I'd do best with confident dog friends who enjoy an energetic play style and don't mind a puppy who's a little too enthusiastic.

I stay busy from morning until bedtime and only slow down when it's time for a well-earned kennel nap. The funny part? The second I hear you moving around again, I'm instantly recharged and ready for another round of fun!

I'm a smart little pup, too. I already know how to sit—especially if you happen to be holding a tasty treat! I'm making great progress with potty training, though I still have an occasional accident as I learn. Leashes are still a bit of a mystery to me, but I naturally love following my people wherever they go.

Loud noises might make me jump for a second, but I'm a confident, curious puppy who's eager to take on the world. With a little training, plenty of exercise, and lots of love, I'll grow into an amazing companion.

If your idea of the perfect day includes puppy zoomies, silly antics, happy wiggles, and a loyal sidekick who's always ready for the next adventure, I can't wait to meet you!

dogs.description_html:
💗 Meet Leslie Lutsen! 💗 Big personality. Even bigger heart.

Hi! I'm Leslie Lutsen, and if you're looking for a tiny best friend with a huge zest for life...I'm your girl!

I was just a tiny, big-eared baby when I was adopted back in October 2025. Sadly, through no fault of my own, I recently found myself back at BARC.

But guess what? I'm back in foster care, and I'm happier than ever! 💕

It only took me a minute to remember that I could do the stairs (I was really little when I left!), and now I race up and down them like a pro.

If there's one thing you should know about me, it's this... ⚡ I am basically the Energizer Bunny!

I LOVE to play! Whether it's chasing my foster brothers and sisters around the backyard, zooming through the house, or making new friends, I'm always ready for my next adventure. Dogs? Love them. People? Love them. Life? I LOVE IT!

When I'm not busy playing, I'm a professional cuddle bug. My favorite place to sleep is snuggled in bed with my people and my foster siblings, but I'm also perfectly happy curling up in the crate beside the bed with whichever pup is keeping me company.

I'm also a pretty big fan of mealtime (because who isn't? 😋), and I'll never say no to a tasty snack.

My foster mom says I've finally grown into my ears...but I still think they're my best feature! 👂💗

I'm looking for a family who wants a happy, affectionate little shadow that will keep them smiling every single day. If you have room in your heart (and maybe a spot on your bed), I promise I'll fill your home with love, laughter, and endless tail wags.

Could I be the newest member of your family?
